what: What were the town's non-union salary grades and step rates in 1995?
why: `salary-schedule` and `report-classification-plan` read Schedule A from the 2010 report and FY2011 onward. The 1995 annual town report does not print it: Article 6 of the May 13, 1995 Annual Town Meeting (PDF p77) substitutes `the Classification & Salary Schedule proposed by the Personnel Board and appearing in the Report of the Finance Committee`, effective July 1, 1995, and the schedule itself is not reproduced. The text was searched for salary schedule, classification, step and grade on every page with text (87 of 90) and returned only that article, a Council on Aging grant paying a part-time salary (p17), the appropriation schedule's salary lines (p51-52), the omnibus salary lines (p76) and Article 7's merit augmentation (p77) (sources/data/report-tables/1995/). — closes: the Report of the Finance Committee to the May 13, 1995 Annual Town Meeting, or the Personnel Bylaw Article XV Classification & Salary Schedule effective July 1, 1995, from the Town Clerk.

what: What did each item of Lunenburg's FY1996 capital plan cost?
why: `capital-plans` holds item-by-item costs. The 1995 annual town report prints the FY1996 capital votes only as article totals: Article 8 ($23,140 by taxation `as appearing in the FY96 Capital Expenditure Budget`, not printed), Article 9 ($155,000 borrowed for a high school roof and a primary school septic system) and Article 10 ($109,000 for items named in prose with no amount each) (PDF p77); the Capital Planning Committee's report (p12-13) names no amounts. Searched for capital plan, capital expenditure and capital budget on every page with text (87 of 90): besides those pages it returned the index (p5), Planning Board prose (p32-33), the high school principal's $50,000 request for next year (p39), the schedule line `Capital Plan Component 43/94` (p52) and article text (p75, p79) (sources/data/report-tables/1995/). — closes: the FY96 Capital Expenditure Budget as presented to the May 13, 1995 Annual Town Meeting, from the Capital Planning Committee or the Finance Committee report.

what: What did each capital project fund article hold and spend in fiscal 1995?
why: `report-capital-projects` reads the capital project fund schedule by article from the 2001-2010 reports. The 1995 report prints the CAPITAL PROJECT FUND only as one column of the combined balance sheet (PDF p49: cash $147,362.69, bonds payable $1,001,475.00, undesignated ($854,112.31)), with no schedule by article: the text was searched for capital project on every page with text (87 of 90) and returned only that column heading. Some capital articles appear as `fwd` lines inside the general fund appropriations schedule (p51-56), which is a different fund. — closes: the Town Accountant's fiscal 1995 capital projects fund detail (balances by article at June 30, 1995).

what: How many weighing and measuring devices did the Sealer test in 1995, and what did sealing bring in by device?
why: `report-weights-measures` holds the Sealer's device counts and fees from the 2010 report. The 1995 annual town report prints no Inspector of Weights & Measures report: its text was searched for weights, sealer and sealing and returned only the appointment (p9), the tax bill line Weights and Measures Inspector 1,070 (p47), the appropriation line (p54), the omnibus line WEIGHTS/MEASURES (p76), the inspector's wage (p84) and the receipts line SEALING FEES $863.00 (p50) (sources/data/report-tables/1995/). — closes: the Sealer of Weights and Measures' 1995 annual report to the Division of Standards.

what: How much of Lunenburg's debt at 30 June 1995 sat inside the debt limit, and how much outside it?
why: `outstanding-debt` reads this from the five-year outstanding-debt summary the FY2011-FY2025 reports print. The 1995 annual town report prints its bonded indebtedness issue by issue (PDF p65) and a repayment schedule (p64) whose interest lines mark three issues `INTEREST (EXEMPTED)`, but no summary by purpose and no debt-limit split: its text was searched for debt limit, outstanding debt and exempt and returned only those lines, the Capital Planning Committee's prose on exempt borrowing (p13), the assessors' exemptions (p46) and the balance sheet's ALLOW ABATE/EXEMPTIONS (p49). — closes: the Town's FY1995 Statement of Indebtedness as filed with the Division of Local Services.
